title: The Business Case Practice

header.html: Explain the purpose of the business case practice; describe its relationships with the principles; explain the purpose of the project brief, business case, benefits management approach and sustainability management approach; define output, outcome, benefit, dis-benefit and business objective; describe the business case lifecycle, aligning products to business objectives and tolerances, and establishing business justification
the official PRINCE2 7 Foundation syllabus (PeopleCert), learning outcome 4.1

html:
1Purpose

The business case practice gives the project a way to judge whether it is (and remains) desirable, viable and achievable, to support decisions about continuing to invest.

Question Meaning
Desirable Do the benefits outweigh the costs, risks and dis-benefits?
Viable Can the project be delivered and the benefits realized?
Achievable Can the products be delivered within constraints (time, cost, quality, etc.)?

Main principle link: ensure continued business justification. The business case is checked at every decision point. [Verify live]

2Key concepts

Term Meaning
Output A specialist product the project hands over (for example, a new system)
Outcome The result of change when people use the outputs
Benefit A measurable improvement perceived as positive by a stakeholder
Dis-benefit A measurable decline perceived as negative by a stakeholder
Business objective A target the organization wants to reach that the project supports
Exam tip

. Output = what is delivered. Outcome = what changes. Benefit = the measurable gain. Dis-benefit = the measurable loss. A benefit comes after the project, through use of the outputs.

3Management products

Product Purpose
Project brief The terms of reference, including the outline business case, used to decide whether to initiate
Business case The justification for the project: reasons, options, benefits, costs, risks, timescale
Benefits management approach How benefits will be measured and realized, and by whom (a PID product)
Sustainability management approach How the project handles environmental, social and economic sustainability targets (a PID product)

4Business case guidance

The lifecycle

Step What happens
Develop An outline business case in the project brief, then a detailed one in the PID
Verify The board checks that it is sound and the project is justified
Maintain Update it with changes, risks and progress; review at each stage end
Confirm After the project, check whether the benefits were realized

[Verify live] the step names.

Alignment and justification

Align products to business objectives and tolerances: every product should contribute to a benefit. Establish justification by showing options considered, costs, benefits, risks and timescale. If the case no longer holds, the board should stop the project.

Exam tip

. Benefits come after the project, when people use the outputs. A question that says benefits are realized on delivery is wrong.

Exam tip

. The outline business case lives in the project brief; the detailed business case lives in the PID.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A new payment system is delivered. Which term describes the system itself?

  • AOutcome
  • BOutput
  • CBenefit
  • DDis-benefit
Show the answer

Answer: B. The deliverable is an output.

S2Which statements are CORRECT? (1) A benefit is a measurable improvement seen as positive. (2) A dis-benefit is a measurable decline seen as negative. (3) An outcome is the product the project hands over. (4) A benefit is realized before any outputs are used.

  • A1 and 2
  • B3 and 4
  • C2 and 3
  • D1 and 4
Show the answer

Answer: A. Statements 1 and 2 are correct definitions.

S3Identify the missing word. The business case practice supports decisions about [ ? ] the investment.

  • AContinuing
  • BHiding
  • CTailoring
  • DDelegating
Show the answer

Answer: A. The business case supports decisions about continued investment.

S4At which point is an outline business case first created?

  • AIn the end project report
  • BIn the lessons report
  • CIn the daily log
  • DIn the project brief
Show the answer

Answer: D. The outline business case is part of the project brief.

S5After the project, the team checks whether promised savings were achieved. Which business case step is this?

  • AConfirm
  • BDevelop
  • CVerify
  • DMaintain
Show the answer

Answer: A. Checking benefits after the project is confirm.

S6Which management product sets out how benefits will be measured and by whom?

  • AThe sustainability management approach
  • BThe product register
  • CThe benefits management approach
  • DThe exception report
Show the answer

Answer: C. That is the purpose of the benefits management approach.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What three questions does the business case answer?

Show the answer

Is the project desirable, viable and achievable?

R2Define an outcome.

Show the answer

The result of change that comes when people use the outputs.

R3Define a dis-benefit.

Show the answer

A measurable decline perceived as negative by a stakeholder.

R4Which principle does the business case mainly support?

Show the answer

Ensure continued business justification.

R5Name the four business case lifecycle steps.

Show the answer

Develop, verify, maintain and confirm.

R6What does the project brief contain about the business case?

Show the answer

The outline business case.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Purpose judge desirable, viable, achievable; support investment decisions
Terms output (delivered), outcome (changed), benefit (gain), dis-benefit (loss)
Products project brief, business case, benefits and sustainability management approaches
Lifecycle develop, verify, maintain, confirm
Principle ensure continued business justification
